title: Pointers and const
recap: A pointer to const restricts changing the pointee through that pointer; a const pointer instead restricts changing the stored address. These are independent qualifications.
Use read-only pointer parameters for source data and writable pointer parameters for destination data. Validate every optional address before mutation.
objectives: Implement the stated behavior for multiple inputs.
Run the visible tests and explain one boundary case.
warnings: The function/type interface is fixed, but implementation syntax is your choice.
Do not remove the visible tests; the checker keeps an independent copy.
Respect the stated input domain and lifetime/range rules.
challenge: Implement copyIfPresent(source,destination). If either pointer is null, return false without changing any object. Otherwise copy the source integer into the destination and return true. source is a pointer to const: do not mutate it. Passing the same object as source and destination is valid.
hints: Check both pointers before any indirection.
Self-copy is allowed and naturally safe.
